summary: Backend testing for iter225: HR reset endpoint + shipments router split (2737 → 6 modules). Verified all critical endpoints across core/items/pallets/packing/airport/public modules. HR reset dry-run, validation, and apply-shape all working. 27/28 passed, 1 safely skipped (destructive apply skipped because active campus has real payslips).
critical_code_review_comments: hr.py reset endpoint uses DELETE with query params — semantically odd for a state-mutating operation with a large payload semantics. Consider POST /api/hr/reset with JSON body for cleaner API contract, though functionally works.

In hr.py:1081, the check `if role not in {'admin', 'system_admin'}` is redundant since require_admin already gates the whole endpoint to admin/system_admin roles — meaning any admin can reset all campuses, contradicting the docstring at line 1032 which says 'all requires system_admin'. If system_admin-only was intended for campus_scope=all, tighten to `if role != 'system_admin'`.
shipments_pkg split verified — 55 @router decorators = 7 (core) + 15 (items) + 11 (pallets) + 14 (public) + 8 (airport). All endpoints reachable. Backend log confirms 'All modular routers loaded'.
Recycle-bin dump in hr reset loops docs one-by-one (line 1177) — for large datasets consider bulk insert_many.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral test shipments (TEST_iter225_*) created and cleaned up in fixtures. No permanent seed data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: HR reset destructive apply test (TestHrResetApplyOnTestData) intentionally skips when active campus has existing payslips (safety). To actually test wipe end-to-end, first create a manual payslip via POST /api/hr/payslips/manual on a fresh/empty campus, then run apply. All 55 shipments_pkg endpoints confirmed live — future refactor tests can reuse this file's fixture pattern.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Initial 4 test failures were payload-schema mismatches in test script (used 'description' instead of 'name', 'kind' instead of 'type', missing passenger_id for suitcase). All fixed and passing.
